studies.Title: Protective effects of plasma carotenoids on the risk of bladder cancer.
studies.Reference: Protective effects of plasma carotenoids on the risk of bladder cancer.
studies.Population: Patients with bladder cancer and healthy controls at Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: We performed a case-control study in 242 patients with bladder cancer and 204 healthy controls at Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center from 1993 to 1997. Epidemiological data and blood specimens were collected on 84 cases and 173 controls.
extraction_supporting_text.cases: Epidemiological data and blood specimens were collected on 84 cases and 173 controls.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: When using plasma levels of micronutrients as continuous variables, the adjusted OR was 0.22 (95% CI 0.05 to 0.92) for alpha-carotene, 0.42 (95% CI 0.18 to 1.00) for lutein, 0.16 (95% CI 0.02 to 1.06) for zeaxanthin, 0.94 (95% CI 0.89 to 0.99) for lycopene and 0.90 (95% CI 0.81 to 1.00) for beta-cryptoxanthin.
extraction_supporting_text.confidence_interval: When using plasma levels of micronutrients as continuous variables, the adjusted OR was 0.22 (95% CI 0.05 to 0.92) for alpha-carotene, 0.42 (95% CI 0.18 to 1.00) for lutein, 0.16 (95% CI 0.02 to 1.06) for zeaxanthin, 0.94 (95% CI 0.89 to 0.99) for lycopene and 0.90 (95% CI 0.81 to 1.00) for beta-cryptoxanthin.
extraction_supporting_text.comparison: When using plasma levels of micronutrients as continuous variables
extraction_supporting_text.design: We performed a case-control study in 242 patients with bladder cancer and 204 healthy controls at Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center from 1993 to 1997.
extraction_supporting_text.timing: We performed a case-control study in 242 patients with bladder cancer and 204 healthy controls at Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center from 1993 to 1997.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_measurement: Plasma micronutrients, including lutein, zeaxanthin, beta-cryptoxanthin, lycopene, alpha-carotene, beta-carotene, retinol, alpha-tocopherol and gamma-tocopherol, were determined by high performance liquid chromatography.
